newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Brittan says ITA huge advance for world economy.
newsitem.headline: Brittan says ITA huge advance for world economy.

text.p: European Trade Commissioner Leon Brittan said on Thursday the 15 member European Union Council of trade ministers endorsed an agreement with the United States on a global information technology pact.

"The basis of what we have agreed with the United States provides for a deal on ITA (information technology agreement) which will be a huge advance for the world economy," Brittan told a news conference.

The European Union and the United States had reached agreement in talks at the ministerial conference of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) that the ITA should cover the bulk of industrial information technology products, and as well as digital photocopiers and capacitors, he said.
However, the agreement did not include consumer electronics and audio materials, he told a news conference on the fourth day of the WTO's inaugural ministerial meeting.
"This is the biggest trade step forward, if it is completed today, that has happened since the end of the Uruguay Round," he said.
U.S. spokesman Jay Ziegler said the critical objective now was achieving agreement from countries representing 90 percent of the trade in the information technology sector.
"This is extraordinarily positive," Ziegler told reporters.

"We have had to work very hard to get to this point. Now the critical objective is to meet the 90 percent product coverage threshold, because if we don't do that the agreement doesn't take effect," he said.
The WTO ministerial meeting ends on Friday.
Brittan said the 90 percent threshold was not "a rigid barrier"

"Clearly, both Europe and the United States made it clear that this is not a bilateral agreement. It's meant to be agreement covering the countries in the world most involved in this whole area of activity," he said.

"Participants will implement the actions foreseen in the declaration providing the participants representing approximately 90 percent of world trade in information technology products have by then, that is by March 15, 1997, notified their acceptance," he said, quoting from the draft declaration agreed by the United States and European Council.
